podcast.body: This song, released in 1972, became one of pop's most famous and best diss records, rising to number one in January 1973. Carly Simon has maintained mystery about the full identity of the "you" it targets, though she clarified it's not about ex-husband James Taylor or Mick Jagger (who sings backup). She later revealed that the middle verse, describing the vain man taking advantage of a naive singer, is about actor Warren Beatty. The song's genius lies in its meta-diss nature, explicitly stating, "I bet you think this song is about you," and its immense popularity, sending her album "No Secrets" to number one. "But your so vain rose all the way to number one in January 1973."
